Rashi on Ketubot 20a:10:1.hebrew: עצמו מאי - אם בעל דין עצמו מזכירו, עד שנזכר, מאי:
Rashi on Ketubot 20a:10:1.english: Himself, what [is the law]? - If the litigant himself reminds him [the witness], and [thereby] the witness remembers, what [is the ruling]?

Rashi on Ketubot 20a:1:1.hebrew: וכשם שאין מזימין העדים אלא בפניהם - שהרי הם באין לחייבן כדי לעונשן — או נפש או ממון — והתורה אמרה "והועד בבעליו", יבא בעל השור ויעמוד על שורו (ב"ק דף קיב:):
Rashi on Ketubot 20a:1:1.english: And just as witnesses are rendered conspiring only in their presence - For they come to obligate them in order to punish them — either [with] life or [with] money — and the Torah stated, "and it has been testified to its owner," [meaning] let the owner of the ox come and stand by his ox (Bava Kamma 112b).

Rashi on Ketubot 20a:1:2.english: So too, they do not contradict [witnesses] - Even to nullify their testimony.

Rashi on Ketubot 20a:2:1.english: They would not pay attention to them - [that is,] to the witnesses of the document, to collect [based] on their testimony.

Rashi on Ketubot 20a:2:2.hebrew: השתא - דאיכא למימר אילו הוו קמן הוו מודו להני, אמרת מהימני:
Rashi on Ketubot 20a:2:2.english: Now - Where one can say [that] if they were before us they would have admitted to these [witnesses], do you say they are believed?

Rashi on Ketubot 20a:3:1.hebrew: ואוקי ממונא בחזקת מריה - בחזקת הלוה, ואם קרקע היא תעמוד בחזקת המוכר. ודקתני בבריי' "אין נאמנים" — לא דליהוי שטרא מעליא למיגבי ביה, אלא דלא קרעינן ליה; ואי תפיס מידי והדר אתי האי ותבע מיניה, לא מפקינן מיניה, דאמרינן: אוקי תרי לבהדי תרי, וממונא בחזקת היכא דקאי:
Rashi on Ketubot 20a:3:1.english: And establish the money in the possession of its owner - In the possession of the borrower, and if it is land, it shall remain in the possession of the seller. And as for what [the baraita] teaches, "They are not believed" — [this does] not [mean] that it should be a valid document with which to collect, rather that we do not tear it up; and if [the lender] seizes something and then this [borrower] comes and claims [it] from him, we do not take [it] away from him, for we say: Set two [witnesses] against two, and [let] the money [remain] in the possession of where it stands.

Rashi on Ketubot 20a:3:2.english: He sold his property - He sold his lands.

Rashi on Ketubot 20a:4:1.english: And we did not say [this] - that we establish the property in the possession of bar Shatya.

Rashi on Ketubot 20a:4:2.hebrew: אלא דאית ליה - בנכסים הללו חזקה דאבהתא, שהיו של אבותיו, דחזקה מעלייתא היא:
Rashi on Ketubot 20a:4:2.english: Only when he has - in these properties ancestral possession, [meaning] that they belonged to his fathers, for it is a valid presumption of ownership.

Rashi on Ketubot 20a:4:3.hebrew: אבל לית ליה בהו חזקה דאבהתא - אלא חזקה דנפשיה, שקנאן הוא והוחזקו בידו. כקנייתו כך מכירתו, ואין חזקתו חזקה לבטל מכירתו:
Rashi on Ketubot 20a:4:3.english: However, [if] he does not have presumptive possession of his fathers regarding them - rather, [he has] his own presumptive possession, in that he purchased them and they became established in his possession. Just as [was] his purchase, so [was] his sale, and his presumptive possession is not a [valid] presumptive possession to void his sale.

Rashi on Ketubot 20a:5:1.hebrew: נהי דהזמה לא הויא - לעונשם, לא נפש ולא ממון; הכחשה הויא לבטל עדותן:
Rashi on Ketubot 20a:5:1.english: Although it is not [effective for] rendering them conspiring witnesses - to punish them, neither [with] capital [punishment] nor [with] monetary [payment]; [nonetheless,] it is a contradiction, to nullify their testimony.

Rashi on Ketubot 20a:6:1.english: One does not ratify a document - from another document.

Rashi on Ketubot 20a:6:2.hebrew: אא"כ קרא ערער - על אותו שטר האחר, והוחזק בב"ד על ידי עדיו. דאי לא קרא עליו ערער, חיישינן דלמא ההוא גופיה מזוייף הוא:
Rashi on Ketubot 20a:6:2.english: Unless [someone] raised a challenge - against that other document and it was upheld in court by its witnesses; for if no one raised a challenge against it, we are concerned lest that [document] itself is forged.

Rashi on Ketubot 20a:7:1.hebrew: משתי שדות - מעדים האלה: אם חתומים על שני שטרות אחרים שהן מכר שתי שדות, ואכלום הלקוחות ע"י שטרות הללו שלש שנים, מקיימין שטר שלישי מהן, אם החתימות דומות:
Rashi on Ketubot 20a:7:1.english: From two fields - [i.e.,] from these witnesses: if they are signed on two other documents that are [bills of] sale for two fields, and the buyers consumed [the produce of] them by means of these documents for three years, we ratify a third document from them, if the signatures are similar.

Rashi on Ketubot 20a:8:1.hebrew: וביוצא מתחת ידי אחר - שהשטרות הללו שמקיימין את השלישי מהם יוצא מתחת ידי אחר, ולא מתחת ידיו של זה המוציא את השלישי:
Rashi on Ketubot 20a:8:1.english: And when [it] emerges from the possession of another - [That is,] these documents from which they authenticate the third [document] emerge from the possession of another, and not from the possession of this [person] who produces the third [document].

Rashi on Ketubot 20a:8:2.hebrew: זיופי זייף - הסתכל בכתב של אותן שטרות, וכוון וחתם הוא עצמו את השלישי דוגמת אותה חתימה:
Rashi on Ketubot 20a:8:2.english: He forged [it] - He looked at the handwriting of those documents, and matched [it] and signed the third [document] himself in the likeness of that signature.

Rashi on Ketubot 20a:8:3.hebrew: מכוין - מצמצם כתב בכתב, הואיל ואינו לפניו:
Rashi on Ketubot 20a:8:3.english: Match [accurately] - Aligning handwriting with handwriting, since it is not before him.

Rashi on Ketubot 20a:9:1.hebrew: כותב אדם - אם עשאוהו עד בדבר וירא לשוכחו, כותבו על חתיכת קלף ומצניעה:
Rashi on Ketubot 20a:9:1.english: A person may write - If [people] made him a witness in a matter and he is afraid of forgetting it, he writes it on a piece of parchment and puts it away.

Rashi on Ketubot 20a:9:2.hebrew: ומעיד - ע"פ אותו כתב אפי' לאחר כמה שנים:
Rashi on Ketubot 20a:9:2.english: And he testifies - Based on that writing, even after several years.

Rashi on Ketubot 20a:9:3.english: That he remembers it on his own - Without seeing the document, he recalls some of his testimony by himself.

Rashi on Ketubot 20a:9:4.hebrew: אע"פ שאין זוכרה מעצמו - אלא לאחר שרואה בשטר, נתן בלבו ונזכר, שלא נשתכח ממנו כל כך, שכשמזכירים לו נזכר. אבל אינו נזכר לגמרי — לא, דרחמנא אמר "מפיהם" ולא "מפי כתבם":
Rashi on Ketubot 20a:9:4.english: Even though he does not remember it on his own - [This means that] only after he sees [the testimony] in the document, he applies his mind and remembers, [for] it was not so completely forgotten by him that, when they remind him, he [still] remembers. But [if] he does not remember it at all — [then he may] not [testify], for the Merciful One said "from their mouths," and not "from their writings."

Tosafot on Ketubot 20a:3:1.hebrew: אלא אמר ר"נ אוקי תרי להדי כו' - וא"ת: ולר"נ אמאי לא מגבינן ביה בשטרא? הא סבר ר"נ כרב הונא (שבועות מז) [ב"ב דף לא:] בשני כתי עדים המכחישות זו את זו, דכל אחת באה בפ"ע ומעידה, אע"ג דלפי עדות כל אחת חבירתה פסולה לכל עדיות; הכא נמי, כיון דאין מכחישין אותן לומר שלא לוה כלום, אלא אומרים: "אינכם נאמנים בדבר זה, דפסולין הייתם", ליתכשרו, ואמאי לא מגבינן ביה בשטר? ויש לומר: דהתם באה כל אחת בפ"ע ומעידה, משום דמוקמינן כל אחת בחזקת כשרות; אבל הכא, שאומרים: "קטנים היו" או "קרובים משנולדו עד עתה שנתרחקו", ליכא למימר אוקמינהו אחזקתייהו, דפסלינן אותן משנולדו. ואנוסים היו נמי מחמת נפשות — לא שייך לאוקמי אחזקה, דהא לא פסלי להו כלל. ורשב"א אומר: דהכא לא מוקמינן להו אחזקה, כדאמר לעיל, משום דאילו הוו קמן — דלמא הוו מודו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 20a:3:1.english: Rather, Rav Naḥman said: Establish two against [the two], etc. - And if you ask: According to Rav Naḥman, why do we not collect with this document? Behold, Rav Naḥman holds like Rav Huna (Shevuot 47) [Bava Batra 31b] regarding two sets of witnesses that contradict one another, that each one comes on its own and testifies, even though according to the testimony of each one, its counterpart is disqualified for all testimonies; here too, since they do not contradict them by saying that [the borrower] did not borrow anything, but rather say, "You are not believed in this matter, because you were disqualified," let them be deemed valid, and why do we not collect with the document? And one can answer that there, each [set] comes on its own and testifies because we establish each one in its presumptive status of fitness; but here, where they say, "They were minors" or "[They were] relatives from when they were born until now, when they became distant," one cannot say "Establish them in their presumptive status," because we disqualify them from when they were born. And [regarding the claim that] they were coerced due to danger to life as well — it is not applicable to establish [them] in a presumptive status [of fitness], for they do not disqualify them at all. And the Rashba says that here we do not establish them in a presumptive status [of fitness], as [Rav Naḥman] said above, because if they were before us — perhaps they would admit [to the second pair].

Tosafot on Ketubot 20a:3:2.hebrew: ואוקי ממונא בחזקת מריה - פירש בקונט': "ואינן נאמנין" דקתני — לאו דמגבינא בשטרא, אלא דלא קרעינן ליה, ונפקא מינה דאי תפס לא מפקינן מיניה. וקשה, דאמר בפ"ק דב"מ (דף ו: ושם) גבי ספק בכור: תקפו כהן — מוציאין אותו מידו; אלמא תפיסה דלאחר ספיקא לאו כלום היא! ומיהו אההוא דסוף השואל (שם דף קב: ושם) לא קשה מידי, דאמרי' גבי משכיר בית לחבירו בי"ב זהובים לשנה, מדינר זהב לחדש: בא בתחלת החדש — כולו למשכיר, אלמא דבחזקת משכיר הוא, ואפ"ה קאמר: בא בסוף החדש — כולו לשוכר; דשאני התם, דכיון דלא בא בתחלת החדש איכא למימר דאודויי אודי ליה. ויש לומר, דשאני גבי בכור שכהן תופס מספק, דאין יודע אם בכור הוא, אבל הכא שטוען ברי — מהניא תפיסה. וא"ת: בחזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף לד:) גבי "זה אומר של אבותי כו'", אמר ר"נ: כל דאלים גבר, ופריך מהמחליף פרה בחמור: "זה אומר ברשותו ילדה וזה אומר כו' — יחלוקו"; ומאי קושיא, הא ההיא אתיא כסומכוס ורב נחמן כרבנן, דלרבנן דאמרי המע"ה היינו דינא דכל דאלים גבר, כיון דמהניא תפיסה כשטוען ברי! ויש לומר דהכי פריך: דאפי' רבנן לא פליגי אסומכוס אלא משום דחד מינייהו מוחזק ואיכא למימר המע"ה, אבל הכא דאין אחד מוחזק יותר מחבירו — מודו לסומכוס דיחלוקו. ועי"ל, דהכא מיירי כשתפס קודם שנולד הספק. ורשב"א נראה לו להעמיד הברייתא בשובר, ולהכי אין נאמנין, דאוקי ממונא בחזקת מריה ומחזקינן עדי שובר בכשרים, ולא יפרע:
Tosafot on Ketubot 20a:3:2.english: And establish the money in the possession of its owner - Rashi explained [that] "and they are not believed" that [the baraita] teaches [means] not that we collect with the document, rather that we do not tear it up, and the practical difference is that if [the lender] seizes [property], we do not take it away from him. And this is difficult, for it says in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (6b, and there [in the parallel passages]) regarding a doubtful firstborn: if a kohen seized it, we take it out of his hand; thus, seizure after a doubt has arisen is of no effect! However, from that [passage] at the end of [the chapter] HaSho'el (there, 102b, and there), there is no difficulty at all, where we say regarding one who rents a house to his fellow for twelve gold coins a year, at a gold dinar per month: if he comes at the beginning of the month, it all belongs to the landlord — thus it is in the landlord's presumptive possession — and even so it says [that] if he comes at the end of the month, it all belongs to the tenant; for it is different there, since he did not come at the beginning of the month, one can say that he conceded to him. And one can say [in resolution of the difficulty from Bava Metzia 6b] that it is different regarding a firstborn, where the kohen seizes out of doubt, for he does not know whether it is a firstborn, whereas here, where he claims with certainty, seizure is effective. And if you ask: in [the chapter] Chezkas HaBatim (Bava Batra 34b), regarding "This one says 'it belonged to my ancestors,' etc.," Rav Nachman said: "Whoever is stronger prevails," and [the Gemara] challenges from [the case of] one who exchanges a cow for a donkey, [where] "this one says 'it gave birth in his possession,' and this one says, etc. — they divide [it]"; and what is the difficulty? Surely that [mishnah] follows Symmachus, whereas Rav Nachman follows the Rabbis, for according to the Rabbis who say "the burden of proof is on the claimant," that itself is the law of "whoever is stronger prevails," since seizure is effective when one claims with certainty! And one can say that this is what [the Gemara] is asking: that even the Rabbis only disagree with Symmachus because one of them is in possession and one can say "the burden of proof is on the claimant," whereas here, where neither one is in possession more than the other, they agree with Symmachus that they divide [it]. And there is another way to answer: that here it is dealing with [a case] where he seized [the property] before the doubt arose. And to Rashba it appears [preferable] to establish the baraita as referring to a receipt, and therefore they are not believed, because "establish the money in the possession of its owner," and we presume the witnesses of the receipt to be valid, and it is not paid.

Tosafot on Ketubot 20a:4:1.hebrew: ואוקי ארעא בחזקת בר שטיא - דוקא בקרקע הוא דאמרינן הכי, אבל במטלטלים אמרינן דהוו בחזקת המוחזק, כדאמר בפרק השואל (ב"מ דף ק.) גבי המחליף פרה בחמור, דפריך: "וליחזי פרה ברשותא דמאן קיימא, ולהוי אידך המע"ה?" ומשני: "דקיימא באגם". אומר ר"י דהכא לא שייך למימר כדאמרי' בסוף קדושין (דף עט:) ובמי שמת (ב"ב דף קנג: ושם): "אם שכיב מרע הוא — עליהם להביא ראיה שבריא היה, ואם בריא הוא כו'"; דבר שטיא דהכא, כיון דעתים חלים ועתים שוטה — אין ראיה ממה שהוא עכשיו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 20a:4:1.english: And establish the land in the possession of bar Shatya - Specifically regarding land do we say this, but regarding movable property we say that it is in the possession of the one currently holding [it], as it says in the chapter HaSho'el (Bava Metzia 100a) regarding one who exchanges a cow for a donkey, where [the Gemara] asks: "Let us see in whose domain the cow is standing, and let the other be [subject to the rule] 'the burden of proof is upon the claimant'?" And [the Gemara] answers: "[It is a case] where it is standing in a meadow." Ri says that here it is not applicable to say as we say at the end of Kiddushin (79b) and in [the chapter] Mi SheMeit (Bava Batra 153b, and there): "If he is a shekhiv mera [deathly ill], it is upon them to bring proof that he was healthy, and if he is healthy, etc."; for bar Shatya here, since he is at times lucid and at times insane, there is no proof from what he is now.

Tosafot on Ketubot 20a:8:1.hebrew: דלמא זיופי זייף - אור"ת, דדוקא היכא שאין אנו מכירין החתימה אלא ע"י דמיון החתימה להחתימה; אבל היכא דמכירין חתימת העדים בטביעת עין, אע"פ שיש לו חתימה אחרת תחת ידו, ליכא למיחש דלמא זייף — דכיון דמכירין החתימה, אם זייף היה ניכר היטב:
Tosafot on Ketubot 20a:8:1.english: "Perhaps he forged [it]" - Rabbeinu Tam says that [this applies] specifically where we do not recognize the signature except by comparing [one] signature to [another] signature; however, where we recognize the witnesses' signatures by visual recognition, even though he has another signature in his possession, there is no concern that perhaps he forged [it], since once we recognize the signature, if he forged [it], it would be clearly noticeable.

Tosafot on Ketubot 20a:9:1.hebrew: ורבי יוחנן אומר אע"פ שאין זוכרה מעצמו - פי': אבל ע"י השטר זוכרה; אבל אם אין זוכרה כלל, לא, דמפיהם ולא מפי כתבם, כדאמרינן פ' ד' אחין (יבמות דף לא: ושם) גבי מפני מה לא תקנו זמן בקדושין, דקאמר: לינחי גבי עדים, אי דכירי ליתו ולסהדו, ואי לא, זימנין דחזו בכתבא ואתו ומסהדי, ואמר רחמנא מפיהם ולא מפי כתבם. וא"ת הכא נמי אמאי לא אסרינן לכתוב עדות על השטר, שמא ישכח לגמרי ואתו ומסהדי מכתבא, כדחיישינן התם? ויש לומר דודאי התם חשו חכמים, לפי שב"ד מוסרין לו השטר, ויסבור שלכך מסרוהו לו שיעיד אפי' לא יזכור; אבל הכא שמעצמו כותב עדותו על השטר, לא חשו חכמים לכך. וא"ת, ואמאי לא מצו חזו בכתבא ולאסהודי? הא תנן בגט פשוט (ב"ב דף קסח.): מי שנמחק שטר חובו, מעמיד עליו עדים ובא לב"ד, ועושין לו קיומו, ומפרש בגמ' מהו קיומו. וכן בהגוזל קמא (ב"ק דף צח.) דאמרינן גבי שורף שטרותיו של חבירו: פטור מדיני אדם כו'. ה"ד? אי דאיכא סהדי דידעי מה הוה כתוב ביה בשטרא, נכתוב ליה שטרא אחרינא. אלמא לא חשבינן ליה מפיהם ולא מפי כתבם. וי"ל דבפ' ד' אחין (יבמות לא: ושם) חיישינן דלמא אתו ומסהדי בסתם כאילו זוכרין העדות; אבל ודאי אם היו מעידין שכך ראו בחתימתן, הא לא חשיב מפיהם ולא מפי כתבם, דעדים החתומין על השטר נעשה כמי שנחקרה עדותן בבית דין, והוי כאילו מעידין: ראינו עדות שנחקרה בבית דין. ואם תאמר: והכא אפילו אין זה זוכרה כלל, מה בכך? יביא שטרו בב"ד. ויש לומר דע"א בשטר לא חשיב שטר, אלא אותו שיש בו שני עדים, דומיא דספר מקנה. והא דאמר בגט פשוט (ב"ב דף קסה.): עד אחד בכתב ועד אחד בעל פה אין מצטרפין, דמשמע הא שנים בשטר, אפילו בשתי אגרות מצטרפין — התם מיירי כגון שהאחד בשטר והאחד בעל פה, לא שאומר שראה הוא המלוה, אלא שראה מסירת השטר מלוה למלוה, דהוי כשנים החתומים בשטר לר"א, דאמר: עדי מסירה כרתי. ועוד דבירושלמי מפרש: עד א' בשטר, היינו ששנים חתומים בשטר וקיימו כתב ידו של אחד, ולא מצאו לקיים כתב ידו של שני. ומ"מ, נהי דעד אחד לא חשיב שטר לענין שאם יבואו עדים ויאמרו כך ראינו בשטר דחשבינן להו כעד מפי עד, עדות מיהא הוי, ויכול לשלוח כתב ידו לב"ד, ולא חשיב מפיהם ולא מפי כתבם, כיון שהוא זוכר העדות. ורש"י פי' בפירוש החומש: מפיהם ולא מפי כתבם — שלא ישלח בכתב עדותו לב"ד. א"נ אומר ר"י דע"א מועיל בשטר, אם יש שני שטרות, בכל אחד חתום עד א', חשוב כשטר שלם. וכ"ת: א"כ בשמעתין יביא כתבו לב"ד אפילו אינו זכור כלל? ויש לומר דלא חשיב שטר אלא כשעשוי מדעת שניהם, מדעת הלוה שהוא חייב, אז חשיב שטר; אבל הכא שכותב עדותו שלא מדעת הלוה, לא חשיב שטרא. והקשה ה"ר שמואל מוורדו"ן דאמר בחזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף מ. ושם): מחאה בפני שנים, וא"צ לומר כתובו. ומה מועיל כתובו, כיון דאין עשוי מדעת המחזיק? ולפי מה שפירשנו דעדות מיהא הוי כל זמן שזוכר, אתי שפיר. מיהו בלאו הכי מתרץ ר"י דגבי מחאה הקילו, שאינה אלא מדרבנן, דהכי נמי הקילו לומר דמחאה שלא בפניו הויא מחאה, אע"פ שלפעמים לא ישמע, וסמכו על זה דחברך חברא אית ליה; וכן במודעא בפני שנים הקילו לכתוב, להציל אנוס מאונסו. ועוד אומר ר"י דלא בעינן דעת שניהם, והכא היה יכול להביא שטרו אם היה כתוב כתיקון שטרות, אבל הכא מיירי שאינו כתוב כסדר השטר, אלא זכרון דברים בעלמא. ומתוך הירושלמי נראה לפ' בענין אחר סוגיא זו, דקאמר התם: רב הונא כרבי, ור' יוחנן כרבנן. פירוש: כשהעדים באים לקיים חתימתן, אם זוכרין המלוה בלא שטר, אפי' לרבי א"צ לצרף עמהן אחר מן השוק, דעל מנה שבשטר הן מעידין; וכשאין זוכרים המלוה אפילו ע"י השטר, אפי' רבנן מודו דצריכין לצרף עמהן, דעל כרחין אין מעידין אלא על כתב ידן. וכי פליגי, היינו כשזוכרין המלוה ע"י השטר: דלרבנן חשיב זכירה, ועל מנה הן מעידין, ולרבי לא חשיב זכירה. ולשון "כותב אדם" לא משמע הכי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 20a:9:1.english: "And Rabbi Yochanan says: Even though he does not remember it on his own" - Explanation: But through the document he does remember it; but if he does not remember it at all, [he may] not [testify], for [the verse says] "from their mouths" and not from the mouth of their writing, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Achin (Yevamot 31b, and there) regarding why they did not institute [writing] a date in betrothals, where [the Gemara] says: Let them leave it with the witnesses — if they remember, let them come and testify, and if not, sometimes they will look at the writing and come and testify, and the Merciful One said "from their mouths" and not from the mouth of their writing. And if you say: Here too, why do we not prohibit writing testimony on the document, lest he forget completely and they come and testify from the writing, as we are concerned there? One can say that certainly there the Sages were concerned, because the court hands him the document, and he will think that they handed it to him for this reason — that he should testify even if he does not remember; but here, where he himself writes his testimony on the document, the Sages were not concerned about this. And if you say: But why could they not look at the writing and testify? Surely we learned in [the chapter] Get Pashut (Bava Batra 168a): One whose promissory note was erased may stand witnesses over it and come to the court, and they make a validation for him, and the Gemara explains what its validation is. And likewise in [the chapter] HaGozel Kama (Bava Kamma 98a), where we say regarding one who burns the documents of his fellow: He is exempt from human law, etc. How so? If there are witnesses who know what was written in the document, we write him another document. Evidently we do not consider it "from their mouths" and not from the mouth of their writing. And one can say that in the chapter Arba'ah Achin (Yevamot 31b, and there) we are concerned that perhaps they will come and testify in a general manner, as if they remember the testimony; but certainly if they were testifying that so they saw in their signatures, this is not considered "from their mouths" and not from the mouth of their writing, since witnesses signed on a document are treated as if their testimony was examined in court, and it is as if they are testifying: We saw testimony that was examined in court. And if you say: But here, even if he does not remember it at all, so what? Let him bring his document to the court. One can say that one witness on a document is not considered a document, but only one that has two witnesses, similar to the "deed of purchase." And as for what is said in [the chapter] Get Pashut (Bava Batra 165a): One witness in writing and one witness orally do not combine, which implies that two on a document, even in two [separate] letters, do combine — there it is discussing a case where one is on the document and one is oral, not that he says that he saw the lender himself, but rather that he saw the handing over of the document from the lender to the borrower, which is like two signed on the document according to Rabbi Elazar, who said: The witnesses of delivery are what effect [the document]. And furthermore, in the Yerushalmi it explains: "One witness in a document" means that two are signed on the document, and they validated the handwriting of one but did not find [a way] to validate the handwriting of the second. In any case, granted that one witness is not considered a document in the sense that if witnesses come and say "so we saw in the document" we consider them like [testimony of] a witness from a witness, nevertheless it is testimony, and he can send his handwriting to the court, and it is not considered "from their mouths" and not from the mouth of their writing, since he remembers the testimony. And Rashi explained in his commentary on the Chumash: "From their mouths and not from the mouth of their writing" — that he should not send his testimony in writing to the court. Alternatively, Rabbi Yitzchak says that one witness is effective in a document if there are two documents, and in each one a single witness is signed; it is considered a complete document. And if you say: If so, in our passage let him bring his writing to the court even if he does not remember at all? One can say that it is considered a document only when it is made with the consent of both parties, with the consent of the borrower who is obligated — then it is considered a document; but here, where he writes his testimony without the borrower's knowledge, it is not considered a document. And Rabbi Shmuel of Verdun raised a difficulty, for [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] Chezkat HaBatim (Bava Batra 40a, and there): A protest before two, and there is no need to say "write it down." And what good is "write it down," since it is not made with the consent of the possessor? But according to what we explained — that it is at least testimony as long as he remembers — it works out well. Nevertheless, even without this, Rabbi Yitzchak answers that regarding protest they were lenient, since it is only rabbinic; for so too they were lenient to say that a protest not in his presence is a [valid] protest, even though sometimes he will not hear, and they relied on this that "your friend has a friend"; and so too with a declaration of duress before two, they were lenient to write it, in order to save one who was coerced from his coercion. And furthermore, Rabbi Yitzchak says that we do not require the consent of both, and here he could have brought his document if it had been written in accordance with the standard form of documents, but here we are discussing [a case] where it is not written in the order of a document, but is merely a record of matters. And from the Yerushalmi it appears to explain this passage in another way, for it says there: Rav Huna [follows] Rabbi, and Rabbi Yochanan [follows] the Rabbis. Explanation: When the witnesses come to validate their signatures, if they remember the lender without the document, even according to Rabbi there is no need to join another person from the marketplace with them, for they testify about the maneh that is in the document; and when they do not remember the lender, even through the document, even the Rabbis agree that they need to join [another] with them, for they are only testifying, of necessity, about their handwriting. And where they disagree is when they remember the lender through the document: for according to the Rabbis this is considered remembering, and they testify about the maneh, and according to Rabbi it is not considered remembering.
